tasks.q: What does a switch use to send data to the correct device on a LAN?
a: MAC addresses
IP addresses
Domain names
Wi-Fi passwords
tasks.fb: A switch reads the MAC address in each frame and forwards it only to the device it is meant for. Routers are the ones that use IP addresses.

tasks.q: The switch in a computer room breaks. What happens to the PCs plugged into it?
a: They lose their network connection, because every wired PC connects through the switch
They carry on as normal, because the router takes over
Only the PC closest to the switch is affected
They automatically move over to Bluetooth
tasks.fb: In a star network every wired device connects through the switch, so if it fails, all the PCs plugged into it are cut off.

tasks.q: Why are the copper wires inside UTP cable twisted in pairs?
a: To reduce interference
To make the cable stronger
So that it can carry light
To make it waterproof
tasks.fb: Twisting the pairs cancels out electrical interference, including crosstalk between the wires.

tasks.q: Why wouldn't you use UTP cable to link two buildings 2 km apart?
a: Each UTP run only works up to about 100 m, so fibre is used for long distances
UTP cable cannot be used outdoors
UTP is more expensive than fibre optic
UTP only works with wireless devices
tasks.fb: The signal in copper UTP weakens over distance, so a run is limited to about 100 m. Fibre optic carries data for kilometres.

tasks.q: What is the main job of a router?
a: To connect different networks and send packets on using IP addresses
To connect devices within one LAN using MAC addresses
To give each network card its MAC address
To store files for everyone on the network
tasks.fb: A router joins networks together, such as the school LAN and the internet, and forwards packets using IP addresses.

tasks.q: The router fails, but the switches still work. What can students still do?
a: Print to the class printer, but not load websites
Load websites, but not print
Neither print nor load websites
Both, exactly as normal
tasks.fb: The printer is on the same LAN, and the switch still links it to the PCs. Websites are on the internet, which can only be reached through the router.

tasks.q: How does fibre optic cable carry data?
a: As pulses of light through glass
As electrical signals through copper
As radio waves
As magnetic signals
tasks.fb: Fibre optic cable sends pulses of light along thin strands of glass.

tasks.q: Which two reasons best explain why the undersea cables that carry the internet are fibre optic?
a: High bandwidth, and it works over very long distances
It is cheap, and it is easy to install
It is flexible, and it uses RJ45 connectors
It uses radio waves, and it needs no power
tasks.fb: Fibre carries huge amounts of data over thousands of kilometres and isn't affected by electrical interference. It is actually more expensive and harder to install than copper.

tasks.q: What does a wireless access point (WAP) do?
a: Lets wireless devices connect to a wired network
Connects the school network to the internet
Stores the files that devices share
Gives each device its MAC address
tasks.fb: A WAP sends and receives radio waves so that wireless devices can join the wired network. It is connected to a switch by cable.

tasks.q: Why does a large school need lots of WAPs rather than one?
a: Each WAP has a limited range and can only serve so many devices
Each WAP only works with one type of device
WAPs only work in the same room as the router
Adding more WAPs makes the school's internet connection faster
tasks.fb: Wi-Fi range is limited and walls weaken the signal, and each WAP can only handle so many devices well. Extra WAPs don't speed up the link from the router to the internet.

tasks.q: What unique address is built into every NIC when it is made?
a: MAC address
IP address
Web address (URL)
Email address
tasks.fb: Every NIC has a unique MAC address set by the manufacturer. IP addresses are given out by the network.

tasks.q: A desktop PC has a wired NIC but no wireless NIC. How must it connect to the school network?
a: With an Ethernet (UTP) cable to a switch
Over Wi-Fi to a WAP
By Bluetooth to a phone
It cannot connect at all
tasks.fb: Without a wireless NIC the PC cannot use Wi-Fi, so it needs a cable into a switch.

tasks.q: A student on a laptop opens a website. Put the request's journey in order.
steps: The laptop sends the request by Wi-Fi to the wireless access point
The WAP passes it along a UTP cable to the switch
The switch forwards it to the router
The router sends it along fibre optic cable to the internet
tasks.fb: The printer and file server are on the same LAN, but a web request doesn't pass through them.

info.title: Server racks
info.text: Servers and switches are bolted into standard-sized racks in a cooled, locked room. Keeping them together makes cabling tidier and the equipment easier to protect.

info.title: Blinking lights
info.text: The small lights next to each switch port show a device is connected, and flicker when data passes through that port. Technicians use them to spot faults.

info.title: Cat5e or Cat6?
info.text: Cat6 cable has tighter twists and better shielding from interference than Cat5e, so it supports higher speeds over short distances.

info.title: Why light stays in the glass
info.text: Light travelling along a fibre keeps bouncing off the inside edge of the glass core, called total internal reflection, so it can travel for kilometres with little loss.
